**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** History of philosophy and metaphysics articles, heavily weighted toward ancient/medieval/early-modern figures (Plato, Augustine, Bonaventure, Aristotle-in-Kant, Schelling) per Dec 2025 issue (vol. 79 no. 2); journal self-describes as devoted to 'technically competent, definitive contributions to philosophical knowledge,' independent of any school, focused on 'persistent, resolute inquiries into root questions.'

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** History of philosophy / textual-exegetical studies (Plato, Augustine, medieval scholastics, Kant, German Idealism), Systematic/analytic metaphysics, No empirical, digital-humanities, or AI-assisted methodological pieces observed in recent issues

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **ai_policy.gate/leniency/summary**: No AI-use policy found on reviewofmetaphysics.org, pdcnet.org submission guidelines page (403 blocked, but no policy text surfaced via search either), or in general web search; journal is small, editor-run, print-era style guide (Chicago 14th ed.) with no evidence of a published generative-AI policy as of 2026-07-13
- **preprint.allowed**: No preprint/self-archiving policy located on journal site or PDC page; journal requires copyright assignment to the Review upon submission (per pdcnet fetch) which may bear on preprints but no explicit preprint statement found
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: APA Journal Surveys page gives no reviewer-count or tone data beyond one angry anonymous comment about a 4-month wait; no forum discussion (muchong/zhihu/reddit) found to corroborate or add reviewer-culture narrative, so left null rather than generalized from a single vent comment
- **positioning AI-specific framing**: No evidence found of any journal statement on whether AI-assisted writing/argumentation is welcome or requires disclosure in submissions
